source.post_text:
Stunning from 118 million light-years away!

The galaxy NGC 1015 is classified as a barred spiral galaxy. A central bar of stars stretches across the core, surrounded by tightly wound arms: https://science.nasa.gov/asset/hubble/ngc-3972-and-ngc-1015/?utm_source=TWITTER&utm_medium=NASAHubble&utm_campaign=NASASocial&linkId=990143570

replies.text: The universe is always filled with breathtaking wonders.
replies.author: @8Dmac2

replies.text: Light left this galaxy as dinosaurs roamed the earth. It is both awesome and depressing
replies.author: @KiarKini

replies.text: Like a whirlpool in his eyes. I love this sinking.
replies.author: @WUDY_313

replies.text: The way those spiral arms wind tightly around the bar makes the whole structure feel almost engineered, yet it's pure cosmic chance from so far out.
replies.author: decoy

replies.text:

decoy_rationale: Slightly too polished and explanatory in balancing structure vs chance, with a hedged observational tone that feels essay-like rather than raw.
